name: MCP23008 8-bit I/O expander
description: Microchip 8-bit I/O expander with an I2C interface (100/400 kHz, 1.7 MHz): eight GPIO pins (GP0-GP7), each an input with optional weak pull-up or an output sinking/sourcing up to 25 mA, plus an interrupt-on-change output. Runs on 1.8-5.5 V (2.7 V or more for 400 kHz I2C). I2C address 0x20-0x27 set by pins A0-A2. Sold as: Adafruit MCP23008 i2c 8 input/output port expander (product 593, bare MCP23008-E/P chip in an 18-pin DIP that plugs straight into a breadboard; also SparkFun COM-15099), pins numbered 1-18 anticlockwise from the notch.
eli5: Gives your board eight extra on/off pins (for LEDs and buttons) using only the two I2C wires.

buildNotes: Pin 1 (SCL) is next to the notch/dot; pins count anticlockwise seen from the top, so VDD (pin 18) is opposite pin 1.
A0, A1, A2 and RESET must never float: tie A0-A2 to GND for address 0x20 (any to VDD to move up to 0x27) and RESET to VDD.
The bare chip has no I2C pull-ups: fit 4.7 kOhm from SDA and SCL to VDD (skip them if another board on the bus already has them).
Put a 0.1 uF capacitor between VDD (pin 18) and VSS (pin 9), close to the chip.
All pins start as inputs (IODIR = 0xFF). Write 0 bits to IODIR (0x00) for outputs, set output levels in OLAT (0x0A) and read pin levels from GPIO (0x09).
GPPU (0x06) turns on weak pull-ups (about 75 uA at 5 V) so a button can go straight to GND; a pressed button then reads 0.
Give every LED its own series resistor; keep each pin under 25 mA and the whole chip under 125 mA.

driver.code:
# MCP23008 8-bit I/O expander (Microchip DS20001919F), MicroPython driver.
# Register map (IOCON.BANK does not exist on the MCP23008; addresses are fixed):
#   0x00 IODIR (1 = input, POR 0xFF)  0x01 IPOL  0x02 GPINTEN  0x03 DEFVAL  0x04 INTCON
#   0x05 IOCON  0x06 GPPU (1 = weak pull-up on, 40-115 uA at 5 V)  0x07 INTF  0x08 INTCAP
#   0x09 GPIO (read = pin levels)  0x0A OLAT (output latch; read = latch, not the pins)
# I2C address 0b0100 A2 A1 A0: 0x20 with A0-A2 tied to GND, up to 0x27.

IODIR = 0x00
IPOL = 0x01
GPINTEN = 0x02
DEFVAL = 0x03
INTCON = 0x04
IOCON = 0x05
GPPU = 0x06
INTF = 0x07
INTCAP = 0x08
GPIO = 0x09
OLAT = 0x0A

INPUT = 1
OUTPUT = 0


class MCP23008:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x20):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def _r(self, reg):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 1)[0]

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val & 0xFF]))

    def _bit(self, reg, pin, on):
        v = self._r(reg)
        v = (v | (1 << pin)) if on else (v & ~(1 << pin))
        self._w(reg, v)

    def setup(self, pin, mode, pullup=False):
        """pin 0-7 (GP0-GP7); mode INPUT or OUTPUT; pullup enables the internal weak pull-up (inputs)."""
        self._bit(IODIR, pin, mode == INPUT)
        self._bit(GPPU, pin, pullup)

    def output(self, pin, value):
        """Drive an output pin high (1) or low (0). Read-modify-write of OLAT, as the datasheet advises."""
        self._bit(OLAT, pin, value)

    def input(self, pin):
        """Logic level on a pin (GPIO register), 0 or 1. IPOL inverts it if set."""
        return (self._r(GPIO) >> pin) & 1

    @property
    def gpio(self):
        """All eight pin levels as one byte (GP7 = bit 7)."""
        return self._r(GPIO)

    @gpio.setter
    def gpio(self, val):
        """Write all eight output latches at once."""
        self._w(OLAT, val)

    def direction(self, mask):
        """Set IODIR in one write: bit = 1 makes that pin an input."""
        self._w(IODIR, mask)

    def pullups(self, mask):
        """Set GPPU in one write: bit = 1 enables that pin's weak pull-up."""
        self._w(GPPU, mask)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from mcp23008 import MCP23008, INPUT, OUTPUT

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
io = MCP23008(i2c, 0x20)
io.setup(0, OUTPUT)              # GP0: LED (through a 330 ohm resistor) to GND
io.setup(7, INPUT, pullup=True)  # GP7: push button to GND
while True:
    pressed = io.input(7) == 0
    io.output(0, pressed)
    print('BTN=%d' % pressed)
    time.sleep_ms(200)
